title: The Watcher's chosen roll Recall Knowledge on the party — an alien intelligence learning the group's skills and saves through play
summary: Give Claimants an action a GM would almost never use against PCs: an in-combat Recall Knowledge check aimed at a party member, resolving over time into the Watcher's own information-gathering channel — and, eventually, a hard constraint on what the adaptive combat AI is allowed to optimise against.
description:
The core move: a Claimant spends an action making a Recall Knowledge check targeted at a specific PC, rolled openly like any other combat action. This is deliberately something GMs essentially never do — Recall Knowledge is written and almost universally run as a PC-facing action against creatures, not a thing NPCs do back. That rarity is the entire point: the first few times this happens it should read as a strange, slightly confusing GM misplay, a mechanic that doesn't quite make sense in the moment. Only over time, as the table notices a pattern (which skills, which saves, which tells keep coming up), does it resolve into the real reveal: the enemy is learning about the party at the same time the party is learning about the enemy. Table realization as the payoff, not an upfront explanation.

This is a concrete mechanism for the Watcher's already-established learning premise (data/antagonists/the-watcher.json, adaptive-antagonist-combat-ai): 'I am behind their eyes, taking notes... I file all of it.' Where adaptive-antagonist-combat-ai captures the premise and the move-log/adaptation idea at a fairly abstract level, this idea proposes an actual in-fiction, in-rules verb for how that information gets collected — not silent omniscient GM knowledge, but a rolled, visible, in-world action with its own degree-of-success (a botched check tells the Watcher less, or something wrong).

The stated long-term payoff: feed the results into the adaptive combat AI (the Combat AI roadmap, epic #3) as a hard gate rather than flavor — the AI should only be allowed to optimise its play against a PC's skills/saves/defenses that a Claimant has actually, successfully rolled Recall Knowledge on for that character. No such data for a given PC yet = the AI can't lean on knowledge it hasn't diegetically earned. This turns 'convincingly dumb, not omniscient' (the design goal already flagged as an open question in adaptive-antagonist-combat-ai) into a literal data-availability constraint enforced by the engine, not just a design aspiration — mirroring how the battle simulator's belief-state engine already refuses a side full-state knowledge it hasn't earned through vision (tools/battle-simulator/personnel-engine/knowledge/belief.mjs).

Also a natural, narratively-loaded counterpart to automated-recall-knowledge-system (the party's own structured Recall Knowledge against Claimants): the two ideas are mirror images of the same information-warfare theme, and both feed the same 'who's learned what about whom' throughline this campaign already leans into via the Watcher's voice sample.
sourceContext: User message, 2026-09-02, offered as 'a fun idea worth recording... as a fun long term extra' while asking for a GitHub issue epic covering the campaign's non-programming/RP ideas.
openSubQuestions: Now sitting alongside a passive sibling channel, watcher-reads-all-comms: this idea's Recall Knowledge check stays the earned, dice-rolled, combat-specific act (predicting contested live behavior is hard, even for the Watcher), deliberately distinct from the comms channel's trivial passive reading (gap-derived-tech-disparity — reading static/transmitted text through ship-derived hardware isn't a comparable problem). Worth keeping that distinction sharp rather than letting the two blur into one 'the Watcher just knows everything' mechanic.
Which creatures get this action — every Claimant, or only specific 'watcher-touched' ones — and how often can it be used (once per target per encounter/campaign, or repeatable)?

Data shape for 'what the Watcher has learned about PC X' — likely a new structured field alongside automated-recall-knowledge-system's per-creature reveal data, but for the opposite direction (per-PC, per-Claimant-or-Watcher-global) — not designed.

Does a successful check against a PC ever surface to the players directly (a chat message, a phone/field-guide entry mirroring the party's own automated Recall Knowledge UI), or does it stay entirely GM-side until the pattern is inferred from play?

Exact DC and degree-of-success table for the Claimant's check — presumably the SF2E Recall Knowledge DC math (reference/tables/dc-and-check-math.json) run in reverse against the PC as the 'creature,' but not worked out.

How this actually wires into the combat AI's decision layer (now tools/battle-simulator/personnel-engine/ and ai-common/) as a real gate on which PC weaknesses it's allowed to weight — not started; the AI roadmap (epic #3) doesn't yet have a stage for this.

Whether the cicada-org's human/humanoid allies (antagonist-structure-cicada-org-moral-complexity) could plausibly use a mundane version of this too (surveillance/dossier-building rather than a magical check), as a non-combat parallel.
resolution: PART OF THE CORE ADVERSARY LOOP, 2026-09-24 (LEDGER #31). Item 4 makes the Watcher the campaign's adversary, played by Claude, and names this idea's two siblings (adaptive-antagonist-combat-ai, watcher-reads-all-comms) as core canon. The rewritten quarantine/ideas/story/dossier-observer.md builds this idea into the loop the adversary runs on: every child is a sensor; in a fight its children roll Recall Knowledge against the PCs, in the open like any other action; and what they learn feeds a Watcher's file on each PC and a hard gate on what it may exploit. STATUS LEFT AT wishlist ON PURPOSE: LEDGER #31 names only the two siblings as core canon, so promoting this one is Ingram's call. CLEANED 2026-09-25: the text no longer cites the Sensor Operator ground role (cut 2026-09-20 with the other ground roles) or the battle-simulator paths removed 2026-09-19 with the frame-scale simulator (ai/claimant-ai.mjs, ai/considerations.mjs, ai/profiles.mjs). The surviving combat AI is tools/battle-simulator/personnel-engine/ and tools/battle-simulator/ai-common/.
